portfolio.week_narrative: Markets hit fresh all-time highs Monday on hopes of a U.S.-Iran peace deal, then reversed sharply Tuesday after April's CPI print came in at 3.8% — the hottest reading since May 2023, driven by oil prices at $101/barrel. The inflation surprise all but eliminated any remaining hope of a 2026 rate cut from the Fed. Despite the broad pullback, NVDA bucked the trend on AI infrastructure momentum, and the S&P held up relatively well given the macro shock. The week ended as a tale of two markets: AI plays holding strong, macro-sensitive names under pressure.

covered_calls.title: Covered Call Strategy
covered_calls.subtitle: Weekly Options Income on Club Holdings
covered_calls.market_iv_context: VIX spiked on Tuesday's CPI print and remains elevated near 20 — above-average implied volatility means option premiums are richer than normal. Hot inflation prints create ideal covered call conditions: elevated IV, range-bound or choppy price action, and a Fed that is in no hurry to move.
covered_calls.covered_call_primer: A covered call means selling someone the right to buy your shares at a set price by a set date. You collect the premium today regardless of outcome. If the stock stays below the strike price, you keep the shares and the full premium. If it rises above the strike, your shares get called away at that price — you still profit, just capped at the strike.
